scope: Papers explicitly referenced in two supplied research discussions and closely connected foundations; not an exhaustive systematic review of the field.

papers.title: Speculative Speech Recognition by Audio-Prefixed Low-Rank Adaptation of Language Models
papers.reading_depth: Bibliography, abstract, core sections and experimental setup checked; no exhaustive close reading or reproduction.
papers.code_note: Do not assume a public checkpoint exists.
papers.evidence_location: PDF Page 1–4, Figure 1, Section 2.2, Eq. (8), Tables 1–3
papers.summary_en: Speculative Speech Recognition predicts an unheard continuation from observed audio and transcript.
papers.method_en: Connect a language model applying voice conditional soft prefix and LoRA to the Conformer-Transducer output. We also propose a learning label alignment that takes ASR errors into account.
papers.evidence_en: Evaluating speech conditional prediction in LibriSpeech and multi-domain experiments. The default SOWER setting is 1 seconds in the future, 8 candidates, and oracle evaluation to select the best candidate a posteriori.
papers.relevance_en: The closest prior work to preparing the next words and verifying them with new audio; it motivates a text-only versus audio-aware forecasting comparison.
papers.limitation_en: The SOWER improvement cannot be translated into a reduction in word confirmation delay in the actual system. This paper distinguishes the problem from general speculative decoding, which reduces the computation of a large model into a small model.

papers.title: Decode Before You Hear: Speculative Listening for Chunk-Interleaved Full-Duplex Speech Language Models
papers.reading_depth: Bibliography, abstract, core sections and experimental setup checked; no exhaustive close reading or reproduction.
papers.code_note: Do not assume a public checkpoint exists.
papers.summary_en: Full-duplex speech-language-model research drafts during idle time before the next audio chunk and verifies after arrival.
papers.method_en: It uses silence hypothesis, next-order branch of the first token, and hypothesis pool between chunks. Only the prefix confirmed by the target model under the new voice is adopted.
papers.evidence_en: Four models of TickTock-Bench report acceleration of speak chunks by 2.6–2.8 times and reduction of decoding delay before response starts. This text uses 1 second chunks and a low-concurrency environment.
papers.relevance_en: Directly relevant to scheduling precomputation during audio waiting and reusing/correcting wrong branches.
papers.limitation_en: Not an experiment in predicting the next words of pure ASR. High output agreement under a silence hypothesis is not future-word accuracy. Lossless refers to preserving target output.

papers.title: SpecASR: Accelerating LLM-based Automatic Speech Recognition via Speculative Decoding
papers.reading_depth: Bibliography, abstract, core sections and experimental setup checked; no exhaustive close reading or reproduction.
papers.code_note: Do not assume a public checkpoint exists.
papers.evidence_location: PDF Page 5 Section V-A/V-B and Figure 11; 6 side ablation
papers.publication: arXiv 2025; DAC 2025 accepted stated in the original text
papers.summary_en: Accelerates speculative decoding using similarity between small and large audio-conditioned ASR paths.
papers.method_en: It combines adaptive draft length, draft recycling, and two-pass sparse token tree and verifies multiple candidate paths in parallel.
papers.evidence_en: 3.04–3.79 times is the result of using Vicuna-13B as a simulated target. The experiment records the Whisper tiny.en/medium.en path on RTX A6000 and then simulates the delay with TinyLlama/Llama/Vicuna.
papers.relevance_en: Draft recycling and branch-budget control are relevant to this project's candidate-reuse policy.
papers.limitation_en: Does not establish forecasting before actual audio arrival. Do not cite its speedups as a deployed Llama-ASR or real-time Mac result.

papers.title: ParaASR: Multi-Token Prediction for Fast and Long-Context LLM-Based Speech Recognition
papers.reading_depth: Bibliography, abstract, core sections and experimental setup checked; no exhaustive close reading or reproduction.
papers.code_note: Do not assume a public checkpoint exists.
papers.summary_en: It is a Multi-Token Prediction system that proposes multiple future tokens simultaneously in LLM-based ASR and adopts the confirmed prefix.
papers.method_en: We propose 6 tokens at once as five future token branches of the 4B decoder. Match basic ASR and MTP through step-by-step learning.
papers.evidence_en: MTP-5 in WenetSpeech meeting evaluation adopts the average 5.0/6 token. RTF 0.0053 is a single H800, single concurrency, 30 second voice 100 evaluation conditions.
papers.relevance_en: Helps balance accepted length, candidate width and rollback cost, distinguishing acoustic verification from linguistic plausibility.
papers.limitation_en: Multi-token decoding with received audio differs from prediction before future audio arrives. Some dataset numbers differ between Tables 1 and 4; record table and conditions with each accuracy comparison.

papers.title: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding
papers.reading_depth: Bibliography/abstract checked; full PDF collected and parsed; no exhaustive close reading or reproduction.
papers.code_note: Do not assume a public checkpoint exists.
papers.summary_en: Foundational speculative decoding: a small draft model proposes candidates for parallel verification by a larger target.
papers.method_en: The target distribution is maintained through adoption and correction sampling using the draft distribution and target distribution.
papers.evidence_en: Targeting T5-XXL, we report 2–3 times acceleration compared to the standard implementation. What is preserved is the generation distribution of the target model.
papers.relevance_en: A starting point for probabilistic acceptance rules in an accept-if-correct, otherwise-correct procedure.
papers.limitation_en: ASR correct answers or audio content that has not yet been heard are not guaranteed. If the input changes, it must be verified again with the target distribution under that input.

papers.title: Accelerating Large Language Model Decoding with Speculative Sampling
papers.reading_depth: Bibliography/abstract checked; full PDF collected and parsed; no exhaustive close reading or reproduction.
papers.code_note: Do not assume a public checkpoint exists.
papers.summary_en: Scores a short draft in one pass and uses modified rejection sampling to preserve the target language-model distribution.
papers.method_en: The target evaluates each draft location in parallel and corrects the rejection location with the residual distribution.
papers.evidence_en: 70B Reports 2–2.5 times decoding acceleration in Chinchilla's distributed environment.
papers.relevance_en: High branch probability alone does not justify commitment; define a separate verification rule.
papers.limitation_en: Results concern a language model with fixed input. Streaming acoustic alignment and newly arriving input are separate issues.

papers.reading_depth: Bibliography/abstract checked; full PDF collected and parsed; no exhaustive close reading or reproduction.

papers.summary_en: Organizes candidate token paths as a tree for parallel target-LLM verification.
papers.method_en: Verification of different prefixes is parallelized using token tree and tree attention mask.
papers.evidence_en: Reports lower latency than prior serving systems in distributed inference/offloading settings.
papers.relevance_en: Relevant to formalizing likely next-word paths through trees, branches and shared-prefix reuse.
papers.limitation_en: This is an LLM serving result and does not directly prove the efficiency of acoustic verification or streaming ASR. As the number of branches increases, memory and verification costs also increase.

papers.limitation_en: Does not address acoustic arrival or word alignment. Distinguish quality-preserving settings from quality/speed trade-offs.

papers.relevance_en: Provides acoustic-alignment foundations for candidate verification when speech frames and words are not one-to-one.
papers.limitation_en: The original setup does not automatically specify a modern causal streaming implementation. Define encoder future context and decoding policy separately.

papers.relevance_en: Foundational material for connecting acoustic evidence and text prefixes before architecture selection.
papers.limitation_en: CTC itself does not guarantee a streaming encoder. Greedy decoders are already very cheap, so the computational savings in candidate predictions may be small.

papers.title: Zipformer: A faster and better encoder for automatic speech recognition
papers.reading_depth: Bibliography/abstract checked; full PDF collected and parsed; no exhaustive close reading or reproduction.
papers.code_note: Initially, links and source connections were checked only. On 2026-11-11, official 66.11M Streaming Zipformer FP32 ONNX weights were evaluated with streaming greedy decoding on all 5,559 test utterances. WER was 3.058/7.820%, near official 3.06/7.79%. This reproduces checkpoint evaluation, not all ICLR 2024 tables/training or our forecaster. [Baseline report](../../docs/baseline_zipformer_2026-11-11.md).
papers.summary_en: Zipformer combines encoder time resolutions to improve efficiency and recognition.
papers.method_en: We propose a U-Net-like multi-frame rate structure, attention weight reuse, BiasNorm, Swoosh activation, and ScaledAdam.
papers.evidence_en: LibriSpeech, AISHELL-1, WenetSpeech compares and discloses icefall implementation.

papers.reproduction_note: The PDF version/hash identifies the source. Original acoustic training and the paper's complete experiments were not reproduced; subsequent public-checkpoint evaluation is documented above.
papers.project_update_en: On 2026-11-12, 4.60M full/band2 forecasters were trained with matched initialization for 100h × 15 epochs on the frozen 66.11M backbone and evaluated on the full test. Band2+gate mean display gain was 89.58/70.28ms over eager native output and 30.32/16.54ms over native probability+gate. Actual test risks differ; this does not establish matched-risk Pareto improvement, faster commitment or reproduction of the original paper's acoustic training. [Conditions and diagnostics](../../docs/zipformer_ours_2026-11-12.md).

papers.reading_depth: Bibliography/abstract checked; full PDF collected and parsed; no exhaustive close reading or reproduction.

papers.summary_en: Original Common Voice paper describes a multilingual corpus built through community recording and validation.
papers.method_en: Describes sentence recording, multi-contributor validation and construction of a public corpus.
papers.evidence_en: The original paper's date/language/hour statistics and 2026 v27 release statistics describe different versions.
papers.relevance_en: A path toward accent/language diversity; first specify language, validated subset and speaker split.
